conventions: A bare place name standing after bo' as the goal of motion (Jerusalem 5.6, Gezer 5.25) is an adverbial accusative of direction: the ASV's supplied to belongs to the name under rule 33 and not to the verb under rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, which reaches only a direct object.
mashach/hekhin X le-melek rendered 'anointed/established X king': the le before melek is its own unrepresented unit (rule 40) and melek takes the bare king; do not give the le an as.

bekha'im → 'the mulberry trees': trees is the ASV's supplied generic and the unit heads on mulberry (rule 31); the supplied the joins the noun (5.23) or, where the article is written, goes to the article (5.24). The margin's balsam-trees is read and set aside (rule 38).
report: Read all 45 candidate groups and the full dump end to end, including the five added units the lemma table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways without the ASV licensing the difference.

Waw: every non-and rendering (Then, So, Nevertheless, for, Now, who, And when) is read off the ASV under rules 14/17/55; the three unrepresented waws (5.8 s012, 5.17 s012, 5.23 s006) are all apodosis waws the ASV opens bare, treated identically.

Articles: the [ha] of 'that day' (5.8) and 'that place' (5.20) are both unrepresented beside the demonstrative under rule 41; 'king David' (5.3) and 'Millo' (5.9) are unrepresented because the ASV writes no the; 5.19's 'the Philistines' has a written article that takes it while the anarthrous occurrences take a supplied the under rule 15. Consistent.
le before melek in 'anointed/established David king' is unrepresented in 5.3, 5.12 and 5.17 alike (rule 40); the resultative hayah le of 5.2 is unrepresented under rule 21. Consistent.

Directional accusative after bo': 'to Jerusalem' (5.6) and 'to Gezer' (5.25) both give the supplied to to the place name under rule 33, the 5.25 review note showing that correction was already made. mulberry trees heads on mulberry in 5.23 and 5.24 alike.

Single-verse judgment calls, each with the competing reading named in its note and left standing: 5.1 'we' on the hinneh suffix with the trailing pronoun resumptive (rule 20's tripartite reading); 5.2 cleft 'it' added beside a written hayah taking 'was' (rule 21's 'it was' is the alternative); 5.8 italic 'smite' added rather than read as a distributed makkeh under rule 34; 5.10 'greater and greater' split term-to-term across halokh and gadol.

BSB disagreements: all are documented convention differences — the resumptive pronoun of 5.1 (rule 22), demonstrative and vocative-free articles (rule 41), silenced datives and resultative le (rules 21/40), the object marker of 5.7 (rule 16) and bare-opened apodosis waws (rule 14). None is a genuine error.
No promotion or amendment: the chapter taught nothing the contract does not already say.
